newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Losses to VSZ shares pull SAX index down 2.06 pts.
newsitem.headline: Losses to VSZ shares pull SAX index down 2.06 pts.

text.p: Major Slovak shares closed mixed in thinner trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, with losses to shares of VSZ steel pulling the SAX index down 2.06 points to 197.76.
VSZ closed down 19 crowns at 601, with its average price -- used for calculating the index -- down 3.06 percent.

"VSZ still appears to be a good share, as the company is fundamentally a good firm, and the issue now has the potential to attract investor interest, though its volatility remains rather high," said Peter Krutil of Creditanstalt.

Brokers said the market's bearish mood was influenced by a similar atmosphere on neighbouring bourses and also by a controversial amendment to the securities law giving the majority shareholders of a publicly traded issue right to cancel trading of the shares on the stock market.
Parliament is expected to discuss the new legislation next Tuesday.
Oil and gas storage firm Nafta led the day's trading on the floor, with 10,011 shares changing hands, closing up 50 crowns at 1,950, but its average price dipped over one percent.
Brokers noted there was low demand for Nafta share at the moment, with offers to sell at about 1,920, but they were optimistic about the issue's potential to increase in the future.
Oil refiner Slovnaft closed unchanged at 890 crowns, after trading only 14 crowns on the floor.
Overall volume rose to 728,672 shares, boosted by direct trades, from 239,782 shares on Wednesday. Turnover increased to 525.87 million crowns, from 303.55 million on Wednesday.
